sources.title: Modification of soft tissue vibrations in the leg by muscular activity
sources.finding: Frequency and damping depend on contraction force and shortening velocity; directional differences were observed.
sources.application: Do not treat passive joint-angle tension as measured active muscle recruitment. No new activation model is claimed.

sources.title: Muscle activity damps the soft tissue resonance that occurs in response to pulsed and continuous vibrations
sources.finding: Increased muscle activity and damping near tissue resonance; natural frequency did not track input frequency in the hypothesized way.
sources.application: Motivates testing damping first rather than a large frequency increase. Does not prescribe the chosen game multipliers.

sources.title: Soft tissue vibrations within one soft tissue compartment
sources.finding: Measured peak acceleration and timing varied across quadriceps locations despite similar dominant frequency; high frequency energy attenuated spatially.
sources.application: Retain regional nodes and continuous weights. No reason to force every node to move identically.

sources.title: Soft-tissue vibration and damping response to footwear changes across a wide range of anthropometrics in running
sources.finding: 32 analyzed runners; gastrocnemius medialis dominant frequency approximately 10.4–10.5 Hz. Paper defines power decay exp(-c*t), amplitude decay exp(-c*t/2).
sources.application: Do not substitute its s^-1 power decay coefficient for dimensionless solver damping ratio. Running impact data are not a direct calibration of low-frequency whole-surface jiggle.

sources.title: Dyna: A Model of Dynamic Human Shape in Motion
sources.finding: Soft-tissue deformation predicted from motion history, body and limb velocities/accelerations and body shape using captured examples.
sources.application: Supports retaining motion history and inertia rather than a pose-only oscillation. Dyna is not integrated in this change.
